User Story: As the agent, I iterate model->tools->results until there are no tool calls, so I drive a multi-step task to completion.
Expected Behavior (from code): Each iteration calls the provider, executes requested tools, feeds results back; ends when the model emits no tool calls.

User Story: As an operator, I cap a turn's iterations, so a runaway turn can't loop forever.
Expected Behavior (from code): max_iterations (default 50) bounds a turn; exhausting it stops with stop_reason=max_iterations.

User Story: As an operator delegating to sub-agents, I want one shared iteration pool, so the whole tree is bounded.
Expected Behavior (from code): An IterationBudget shared by parent + sub-agents; each iteration draws one unit; empty pool stops the turn; also caps child count.

Expected Behavior (from code): max_cost_usd / max_tokens accumulate across the tree; crossing a ceiling stops with stop_reason=budget_exhausted (non-vetoable).

User Story: As an operator, I want identical repeated tool batches stopped, so the agent doesn't burn budget repeating itself.
Expected Behavior (from code): Same tool batch >=3x in a row stops with doom_loop; fires before execution so exact repeats never run again; one recovery nudge first if budget allows.

User Story: As an operator, I want a struggling agent to escalate nudge->narrow->step-back->stop, so it investigates and re-checks its assumptions before giving up.
Expected Behavior (from code): Multi-signal stuck detector (repeated batch / all-errors / repeated-failure / no-progress) escalates: nudge, then read-only narrow, then a once-per-turn step-back reassessment (streak resets; premise re-verified with read-only probes), then stop with stop_reason=stuck.

User Story: As a user, I want a context-overflow to self-heal, so a too-long prompt doesn't crash the turn.
Expected Behavior (from code): A ContextWindowExceeded error forces a compaction and retries the same call in place (bounded), else ends as provider_error.

User Story: As an operator, I want a stable cacheable prompt prefix, so prompt-cache hits stay high across turns.
Expected Behavior (from code): Two-tier prompt: stable (identity, tool cheat-sheet, safety) + dynamic (env, context) split by a boundary marker so context changes don't invalidate the cache.

User Story: As an operator, I author self.md, so the agent adopts my persona/framing.
Expected Behavior (from code): A self.md in the workspace replaces the default identity line at the top of the stable prompt tier.

User Story: As a user, I want AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/ZAK.md and README folded in, so the agent knows my project's conventions.

Expected Behavior (from code): PRE_TOOL_USE hooks run before execution; can veto (block) or rewrite args; rewrites re-check the never-waivable floors.

Expected Behavior (from code): A batch where every call is READ_ONLY_SAFE + READ_ONLY tier runs concurrently; anything else runs sequentially; result order preserved.

User Story: As a user on a weak model, I want files re-read after a write, so the model sees ground truth not its own claim.

Expected Behavior (from code): When verify_command is set and code changed, the turn can't end completed until it runs successfully; bounded, else verification_failed.

User Story: As a user, I want open plan steps finished before completion, so the agent doesn't abandon a plan.
Expected Behavior (from code): At completion, an unfinished plan triggers a nudge to finish/mark steps; bounded; past the cap the turn completes flagged degraded.

User Story: As a user, I want an abandoned plan auto-dropped, so a stale plan stops nagging.
Expected Behavior (from code): A plan byte-identical across >=3 turn-starts (never advanced) is dropped as abandoned; signature resets on any edit.

Expected Behavior (from code): With require_plan on and no plan yet, the first mutating batch is withheld with a plan-first nudge; read-only never gated; fail-open past the cap.

User Story: As an operator, I want passing-but-weak output refined, so quality clears a bar before shipping.
Expected Behavior (from code): With quality_gate on, after the verifier passes the result+written code is scored on a rubric; below threshold sends the agent back; bounded; fail-open.

User Story: As an integrator, I want a Stop-hook that can keep the turn going, so an autonomous driver can continue.
Expected Behavior (from code): TURN_END hooks at a vetoable stop (completed/doom_loop/stuck) may veto and re-enter with a continuation, up to turn_end_veto_budget.

User Story: As an integrator, I want an observe-only turn-end hook, so logging fires every turn regardless of veto budget.
Expected Behavior (from code): Observe-only TURN_END hooks fire on every turn end (any stop reason, any budget); errors fail open.

User Story: As a user, I want a struggling turn promoted to the deep model, so it can recover.
Expected Behavior (from code): A struggle signal (doom/stuck/verify-failed) latches the turn to the deep_code model for the rest of the turn.

User Story: As an operator, I want a failed model swapped out, so a provider outage doesn't end the turn.

Expected Behavior (from code): RateLimited calls retry with jittered exponential backoff honoring Retry-After inside the fixed _RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_HORIZON (ADR-0014).

User Story: As a user, I want the session saved at message boundaries, so a crash/cancel never leaves inconsistent state.
Expected Behavior (from code): The session persists after each message add (never mid-iteration); a cancelled turn is saved before raising.

User Story: As an operator, I want spend attributed per model, so /cost shows quick-vs-deep breakdown.
Expected Behavior (from code): Every call's Usage is tagged with the model id and folded into session + budget; /cost can group by model.

User Story: As an operator debugging, I want a per-turn decision trace, so I can see every routing/recovery move.
Expected Behavior (from code): With trace_dir set, an append-only JSONL of routing + gate/recovery interventions + the final stop is written per turn; best-effort.

User Story: As an operator, I want provider keys hidden from shell children, so a script can't leak my keys.
Expected Behavior (from code): Provider API-key env vars are scrubbed from subprocess children unless subprocess_inherit_provider_keys is set.

Expected Behavior (from code): With egress_proxy on, subprocess traffic routes through a localhost allowlisting proxy (egress_allowed_domains); empty list denies all.

User Story: As a user, I want N isolated retries on a stalled turn, so a flaky task still lands a verified result.
Expected Behavior (from code): With best_of_attempts>1 + verify_command, a stalled turn copies the workspace N ways, runs the verifier in each, and applies the first verified diff back.

User Story: As a user, I want a multi-part ask tracked as plan steps, so an interruption or resume never silently drops half my request.
Expected Behavior (from code): A message naming >=2 registry-known skills seeds one plan step per skill at turn entry; at completion a one-shot nudge names any requested skill neither run via use_skill nor covered by the plan (ADR-0017).

User Story: As a user, I want a repetition-looping model cut off and retried, so a bad sample costs seconds instead of a screen of garbage.
Expected Behavior (from code): A completion whose tail repeats one short chunk is discarded before the transcript and retried once behind a corrective rail; a second conviction ends the turn honestly as degenerated (streaming probes cut a runaway stream mid-flight; tool-calling batches are never judged) (ADR-0018).

User Story: As a user, I want the agent to notice when it paves over a contradiction, so a surprising file-not-found gets diagnosed instead of silently recreated.
Expected Behavior (from code): A successful write_file to a path whose read_file errored earlier the same turn carries a [harness] note asking the model to diagnose the mismatch or confirm the create was intentional; once per path per turn, per-turn memory, relative/absolute spellings canonicalized, zero extra iterations (ADR-0020).

User Story: As a user, I never want the agent to mistake a harness nudge for me speaking, so its replies stay honestly attributed.
Expected Behavior (from code): Every loop-injected directive renders as '[harness] Hint: ...' via _control_rail, and the system prompt defines the [harness]/[hook]/[plan] tag family once (automated output; never attribute to the user; never apologize — act) (ADR-0021).

User Story: As an operator, I pick a posture (deny/ask/acceptEdits/allow/autonomous), so I control how much auto-runs.
Expected Behavior (from code): Five modes order how much auto-allows; ask is the safe default; autonomous auto-allows but hard-denies dangerous patterns without prompting.

User Story: As an operator, I want every privileged call authorized first, so nothing dangerous runs unchecked.
Expected Behavior (from code): Each tool declares a tier; the policy checks tier-vs-mode, then dangerous patterns, dependency gate, protected paths -- checks only tighten.

User Story: As an operator, I want catastrophic commands blocked, so 'rm -rf /' / sudo / fork bombs can't run.
Expected Behavior (from code): 14 built-in regexes escalate a match to ask (hard-deny in autonomous/deny); operator regexes can only tighten.
Notes: ux: rm -rf <relative/path> over-blocked (regex matches any slash); hard-deny in autonomous, so an unattended agent cannot delete a relative subdir. Also: 15 patterns not 14.

User Story: As an operator, I want writes to .git/.env/.venv blocked, so repo/secrets/deps aren't clobbered.
Expected Behavior (from code): A write whose path matches a protected pattern never auto-allows -- escalates to ask (hard-deny in autonomous). Tier-aware since ADR-0028: READ_ONLY tools skip the write-sensitive built-ins (.git/, venv are readable) but secrets (.env) and operator env regexes bind reads too; denial messages say read/write accurately. Settings-ingested denies keep their verb (ADR-0030): a deny Read(glob) binds reads+writes, a deny Edit/Write(glob) binds writes only. Relative path arguments also match in their workspace-resolved absolute form (ADR-0031), so a relative spelling cannot bypass a parent-prefixed glob. .claude/ is NOT a built-in class since ADR-0029: the agent's config (skills, rules, CLAUDE.md, the settings files) is agent-editable, and the workspace's always-ingested permissions deny rules are the sole authority over it.

User Story: As an operator, I want installs of undeclared packages flagged, so typosquatting can't sneak in.
Expected Behavior (from code): When enabled, a pip/npm install of a package not in the manifests escalates (hard-deny in autonomous).

User Story: As a user, I want 'allow for session' to persist, so I'm not re-asked every call.
Expected Behavior (from code): ALLOW_SESSION grants persist for the conversation (honored only if mode is at least as loose as when granted); never waive the floors.

User Story: As an operator, I force a re-prompt for a named tool (e.g. web_fetch), so a sensitive tool always asks.
Expected Behavior (from code): Tools in confirm_tools escalate to ask every call regardless of tier; session-grantable; can only tighten.

User Story: As an operator, I trust/distrust a specific tool, so I can loosen or tighten it independently.

User Story: As the agent, I install a missing zakcode optional dep into zakcode's own interpreter, so a broken optional capability is a one-command self-fix.
Expected Behavior (from code): Declared-package set unions harness_declared_packages() (zakcode's own dist requirements, every extra) with workspace manifests; pip_install_hint's exact command passes the gate in autonomous; unvetted packages still deny (ADR-0019).

User Story: As the agent, I read a workspace file (optionally line-sliced), so I can inspect code.
Expected Behavior (from code): Reads a UTF-8 file within the workspace, optional 1-based offset/limit, ~100KB cap with truncation notes; errors cleanly out-of-workspace.

Expected Behavior (from code): Replaces old_string (one or all); idempotent no-op if already applied (distinctive new_string present); same write firewalls.

User Story: As the agent on Windows, I run PowerShell, so I can use PS cmdlets.
Expected Behavior (from code): Prefers pwsh, falls back to powershell.exe; same cwd/timeout/cap; same dangerous-pattern gating.
Notes: ux: powershell 60s timeout hard ceiling, same as bash.

User Story: As the agent, I list a directory, so I can explore the tree.
Expected Behavior (from code): Lists entries (dirs suffixed /), up to 1000 shown; respects .git/.gitignore/.zakcodeignore unless include_ignored.

User Story: As the agent, I match files by glob, so I can find files by name.

Expected Behavior (from code): read_xlsx/read_docx extract data; create_xlsx/create_docx build documents atomically; downloadable artifacts; size-capped.

User Story: As an operator, I opt into model ranking, so relevance is smarter.
Expected Behavior (from code): context_classifier=model scores all candidates in one cheap batched call per turn; falls back to heuristic on failure.
Notes: ux: context_classifier is an unvalidated free string; a typo silently falls back to the heuristic with no warning.

User Story: As an operator, I rank with my own trained model, so relevance is tuned to my workloads.
Expected Behavior (from code): context_classifier_weights loads a RelevanceModel (logistic regression) scoring candidates; guards a feature-set mismatch; fail-soft.

User Story: As an operator, I log offered-vs-used context, so I can train a ranker.
Expected Behavior (from code): context_signal_log appends per-turn JSONL of offered candidates + whether each was used; observe-only turn-end hook; best-effort.

User Story: As an operator, I want 'used' labelled cheaply by default, so logging adds no spend.
Expected Behavior (from code): Default: a ref is used if it appears (path-normalized) in a tool-call arg or the assistant text; blind to in-context use.

User Story: As an operator, I want 'used' to catch in-context use, so the label isn't biased against injected content.
Expected Behavior (from code): context_signal_judge labels used via a cheap model judging which offered items the response drew on; unions the proxy; fail-soft.

User Story: As an operator, I train a ranker from my log, so I can deploy it.
Expected Behavior (from code): train_relevance fits a pure-Python logistic regression on the signal log (no ML deps); empty/garbage log -> default prior.

User Story: As an integrator, I want session-boundary hooks, so I can prime/serialize/encode my framework state.
Expected Behavior (from code): SESSION_START (once), PRE_COMPACT, SESSION_END, ON_SKILL_SELECTED fire observe-only; failures isolated.

User Story: As an integrator, I register a recall hook, so my memory is folded into each turn.
Expected Behavior (from code): register_context hooks return text injected as a fenced untrusted ephemeral tail message (prompt-cache safe).

User Story: As an operator, I configure shell hooks in .claude/settings.json, so I reuse Claude-Code-style hooks.
Expected Behavior (from code): Hook specs ALWAYS load from .claude/.zakcode settings.json at Agent construction (event-name mapped) - no adoption flag or folder-trust prompt exists (ADR-0025); dangerous commands gated (hard-denied in autonomous); provider keys scrubbed.

User Story: As an integrator, I write a shell hook, so a script can gate/observe.
Expected Behavior (from code): Shell hooks get a JSON payload on stdin; exit 0 allow / 2 block; stdout JSON may rewrite args (Zak-native or Claude-Code shape).

User Story: As an operator, I load trusted plugins, so I extend the agent without editing core.
Expected Behavior (from code): Plugins discovered from entry-points/user/workspace; loaded only if enabled AND trusted; untrusted code not imported until the gate passes.

User Story: As a plugin author, I register tools/commands/hooks, so I extend the agent through a narrow surface.
Expected Behavior (from code): PluginContext.register_tool/command/hook; contributions tracked per plugin; a report records loaded/skipped/failed.

User Story: As a user, I drop a SKILL.md, so a reusable procedure is available.
Expected Behavior (from code): Discovers SKILL.md from bundled/user/.zakcode/.claude (later overrides), parses L0 metadata eagerly, lazy-loads the body; malformed recorded not fatal.

User Story: As the model, I want a skills catalog in the prompt, so I know what I can invoke.
Expected Behavior (from code): name+description rendered into the stable (cached) prompt tier; the body loads on demand via use_skill.
Notes: logistical: skills catalog overloads the extra_instructions slot; an injected prompt_builder that sets it silently drops the catalog while use_skill still advertises skills.

User Story: As an operator, I author always-on rules, so the agent follows my standing guidance.
Expected Behavior (from code): *.md rules from bundled/user/.zakcode/.claude render into the stable prompt tier; per-file 8KB + total 32KB caps.

User Story: As a user, I add extra trusted roots, so file tools can reach cross-repo paths.
Expected Behavior (from code): extra_workspace_roots widen the file-tool sandbox; path-escape guard checks all roots.

User Story: As a user, I run `zakcode cli`, so I get an interactive agent session.
Expected Behavior (from code): Starts the REPL: welcome banner, daily tip, `>` prompt; streams responses; supports slash commands + free text; Ctrl-C interrupts.

User Story: As a user, I run `zakcode info`, so I see my resolved config + which keys are present.
Expected Behavior (from code): Prints model/provider/workspace/permissions and provider-key presence (never the key values).

User Story: As a user, I run `zakcode version`, so I know the installed version.
Expected Behavior (from code): Prints the installed version string.

User Story: As a developer, I run `zakcode eval`, so I verify behavioral invariants offline.
Expected Behavior (from code): Runs the hermetic probe suite, prints PASS/FAIL per probe, exits non-zero on any failure; -v shows detail.

User Story: As an operator, I run `zakcode webapp`, so I expose the HTTP/SSE/WS API.
Expected Behavior (from code): Starts the FastAPI server on --host/--port; requires auth for non-loopback unless --insecure; shows a startup banner.

User Story: As a user, I pass --model, so I choose the model (incl. auto/zakpick).
Expected Behavior (from code): Overrides default_model; shown in the banner.
Notes: logistical: --model shown in the banner but ServerClient never sends it; the banner misreports the running model in --server mode.

User Story: As a user, I pass --workspace, so the agent operates on a chosen repo.
Expected Behavior (from code): Overrides the workspace root for tools + session ops.

User Story: As a user, I pass --session, so I resume a prior conversation.
Expected Behavior (from code): Loads the saved session by id and continues it.
Notes: logistical: --session/-s resume is a dead no-op; the CLI never passes session_store, so no session persists to disk. Resume non-functional despite core + SessionStore being implemented.

User Story: As a user, I pass --server, so the CLI drives a remote engine.
Expected Behavior (from code): The CLI becomes a thin SSE client of a remote zakcode webappr; same renderer; headless permission prompts fail closed.
Notes: ux: --server silently ignores --workspace/--session/--no-rules/--skill-dir/--extra-root/--trace with no warning.

User Story: As a user, I pass --no-rules, so I disable always-on rules for a run.
Expected Behavior (from code): Turns off rules discovery/injection (default on).

User Story: As a user, I pass --skill-dir, so I add a skills directory.
Expected Behavior (from code): Adds a directory scanned for SKILL.md (repeatable); the dir's repo root + local-paths.conf paths become extra roots.

User Story: As a user, I pass --extra-root, so file tools can reach another path.
Expected Behavior (from code): Adds a trusted workspace root (repeatable).

User Story: As a developer, I pass --trace, so I capture per-turn decision traces.
Expected Behavior (from code): Writes JSONL traces to .zakcode/traces (or ZAKCODE_TRACE_DIR); shows the trace dir on startup.

User Story: As a user, I type /help, so I see the available commands.
Expected Behavior (from code): Prints grouped slash-command reference; notes Ctrl-C interrupts and free text talks to the agent.

User Story: As a user, I type /model, so I see the active model / routing.
Expected Behavior (from code): Shows the model id, or the zakpick routing table + how to assign models.

User Story: As a user, I type /cost, so I see token+cost usage.
Expected Behavior (from code): Shows cumulative tokens (total/prompt/completion), USD cost, cached tokens, and a per-model breakdown when multiple were used.

User Story: As a user, I type /permissions, so I see my posture + grants.
Expected Behavior (from code): Shows the active mode + session allow/deny grants.

User Story: As a user, I type /hooks, so I see configured hooks.
Expected Behavior (from code): Lists shell hooks (event + command) and a count of in-process hooks; dim notice if none.

User Story: As a user, I type /agents, so I see delegatable sub-agent types.
Expected Behavior (from code): Lists sub-agent types (default marked); dim notice if delegation off.

User Story: As a user, I type /plan, so I get a read-only plan without execution.
Expected Behavior (from code): Spawns a read-only planner sub-agent (no write tools); prints the plan for review; not auto-executed.

User Story: As a user, I type /mcp [connect], so I list/connect MCP servers.
Expected Behavior (from code): Lists configured MCP servers + errors; /mcp connect spawns them and registers tools (gated).

User Story: As a user, I type /plugins, so I see plugin status.
Expected Behavior (from code): Lists loaded (with contribution counts) / skipped (reason) / failed (error) plugins.

User Story: As a user, I type /skills, so I see discovered skills.
Expected Behavior (from code): Lists skills + descriptions, hint to invoke via /<name>, invocation count, discovery errors.

User Story: As a user, I type /compact, so I free up context.
Expected Behavior (from code): Summarizes older history into a summary; notice if nothing to compact.

User Story: As a user, I type /clear, so I start fresh.
Expected Behavior (from code): New Agent + session id, reset counters, same model/workspace/settings.

User Story: As a user, I type /exit, so I leave cleanly.
Expected Behavior (from code): Closes the session and exits the REPL.

User Story: As a user, I type /<skill>, so I load a skill's instructions.
Expected Behavior (from code): Loads the skill body into the session as ephemeral context for the next turn; error notice if it fails to load.

User Story: As a user, I want a readable streamed layout, so output is legible.
Expected Behavior (from code): Hanging-indent grid: block markers, receipt connectors with durations, rail bars (red on error); code fences held until complete.

User Story: As a user, I want a thinking indicator, so I know it's working.
Expected Behavior (from code): A transient spinner with a rotating gerund + elapsed time; disabled off-tty / legacy console / ZAKCODE_NO_SPINNER; pauses for prompts.

User Story: As a user, I want a clear approve/deny prompt, so I control escalated calls.
Expected Behavior (from code): Shows tool+args+blast-radius+reason and 3 options (allow once/session, deny); accepts numbers/letters/phrases; unknown/non-interactive denies.

User Story: As a user, I want a startup banner, so I see model/workspace/permissions/session.
Expected Behavior (from code): One-shot box: brand, model (or 'zakpick - picks per task'), workspace, permissions, session id, help hint, daily tip.

User Story: As a user on a constrained terminal, I want ASCII fallback, so output isn't mojibake.
Expected Behavior (from code): Tries UTF-8; falls back to ASCII glyphs on cp1252; ZAKCODE_ASCII forces ASCII.

User Story: As an operator, I want the turn footer to show how much of the prompt was served from cache, so a big token number reads as its real cost and a caching failure is visible at a glance.
Expected Behavior (from code): When the backend reports cache-read tokens, the footer's token item appends (N% cached) — share of prompt tokens; silent at zero (ADR-0021).

User Story: As an orchestrator, I probe /health, so I know the server is live.
Expected Behavior (from code): Returns status+version; the only endpoint exempt from bearer auth.

User Story: As a client, I GET /config, so I read non-secret settings.
Expected Behavior (from code): Returns resolved settings with api_key stripped and credentials masked from api_base.

User Story: As a client, I GET /tools, so I discover tool schemas.
Expected Behavior (from code): Lists tool definitions (name, description, tier, concurrency, params).

User Story: As a client, I create/list/fetch/delete sessions, so I manage conversations.
Expected Behavior (from code): POST/GET /sessions, GET/DELETE /sessions/{id}; corrupt sessions skipped in listing; double-delete harmless.
Notes: note (low, FIXED): added a test for the corrupt-session-skip listing behavior (code was already correct).

User Story: As a client, I POST /chat, so I run one turn and get the full result.
Expected Behavior (from code): Runs a buffered turn; returns text/tool_results/usage/cost/stop_reason/iterations; 409 if a turn is inflight on the session.

User Story: As a client, I POST /chat/stream, so I stream a turn over SSE.
Expected Behavior (from code): Streams AgentEvent frames as SSE; persists even if the client disconnects; 409 if inflight.

User Story: As a client, I POST /complete, so I get a session-less schema-valid completion.
Expected Behavior (from code): Tool-less, loop-less, session-less; validates the schema first; returns data+text+usage; provider error -> 502.
Notes: secret-leak: redact_secrets does not strip URL userinfo (user:password@host), so a credentialed api_base leaks the password in error bodies/logs and ChatResponse.error.

User Story: As a web client, I open a WebSocket, so I get bidirectional input/interrupt/approval.
Expected Behavior (from code): Client sends input/interrupt/approval; server streams events + out-of-band permission requests; one turn at a time; 120s approval timeout.

User Story: As a web user, I upload a file + download artifacts, so I can work with files.
Expected Behavior (from code): POST uploads (base64/data-url, <=50MB, sanitized, atomic, workspace-bounded); list + digest-verified download of artifacts.
Notes: note (low, FIXED): upload dir now keyed by the FULL session.id (was [:8] -- an 8-hex prefix collision shared a dir).

User Story: As a web client, I fetch the event schema, so I stay in lockstep with the wire.
Expected Behavior (from code): Publishes the AgentEvent JSON Schema from the same adapter that serializes frames.

User Story: As a user, I open /, so I get a browser UI.
Expected Behavior (from code): Serves index.html (pure event renderer) mounted after the API routes.

User Story: As an operator, I set ZAKCODE_AUTH_TOKEN, so the server requires a token.
Expected Behavior (from code): Bearer header on every request (except /health), constant-time compare; WS via Authorization or Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol.

User Story: As an operator, I want one turn per session at a time, so concurrent turns can't corrupt state.
Expected Behavior (from code): A shared inflight set makes REST + WS refuse 409 when a turn is already running on that session.

User Story: As a user, I want sessions saved durably, so /resume works and a crash is recoverable.
Expected Behavior (from code): Atomic temp+replace JSON under the client's store (~/.zakcode/sessions for the terminal client; <workspace>/.zakcode/sessions for webapp — ADR-0032); load validates the id (no traversal); corruption never deletes/rewrites the file.

User Story: As an operator, I want forward-compatible session files, so an older file still loads.
Expected Behavior (from code): Accepts schema version <= current; rejects newer as a version error; never destroys on error.

User Story: As an operator, I configure via env/.env, so I control the engine without code.
Expected Behavior (from code): Precedence: defaults -> ~/.zakcode/.env -> workspace .env -> env -> overrides; .env exported so provider keys reach litellm; secrets excluded from dumps.

User Story: As the CLI, I drive a remote server, so --server works.
Expected Behavior (from code): ServerClient health/create_session/astream_turn over HTTP+SSE; same AgentEvent contract as in-process.
Notes: logistical: ServerClient has no bearer-token path, so chat --server cannot talk to a server with ZAKCODE_AUTH_TOKEN set (every call 401s).

User Story: As an operator on a small-window model, I want compaction to never overflow itself, so context recovery actually recovers.
Expected Behavior (from code): Summarize raw in one call while history fits 0.7x the summarizer window; above that render to labeled text and summarize in 0.5x-window slices (2 chars/token floor) with a single fold pass; compact_now returns False on summarize failure instead of raising inside the recovery handler.

User Story: As a framework author, I want the Claude Code compaction hook contract, so serialize-then-restore works across compaction.
Expected Behavior (from code): Every successful compaction (threshold auto / reactive recovery / manual /compact) fires SessionStart(source=compact) after the rewrite; PreCompact trigger says auto for threshold+recovery and manual only for /compact.

User Story: As an operator, I want to see every compaction with its size, so a transcript rewrite never reads as silent memory loss.
Expected Behavior (from code): Proactive compaction yields a status notice (context near the window - compacted N -> M messages) and records a trace note; the reactive notice carries before -> after counts.

User Story: As an operator on a small-window model, I want one verbose tool result to never sink the session, so long tasks survive on 131k local pods.
Expected Behavior (from code): Each result's model-facing text is clamped at context_window x 0.25 x 3 chars (32k window assumed when undeclared) with a head-heavy head+tail keep and an elision note naming the remedy; hook notes and rails append after the clamp so guidance is never elided; PostToolUse hooks still receive the full output.

User Story: As an operator on a small model, I want garbage tool calls stopped before they execute, so degeneration becomes a recovery nudge instead of executed nonsense.
Expected Behavior (from code): burst_repetition convicts >=12 consecutive repeats (>=150 chars) of one 2-64 char unit anywhere in the JSON-encoded arguments (single-char runs never convicted); the call is vetoed before the permission gate with a Fix rail naming the fragment; the struggle flag latches.

User Story: As a user, I never want the agent to call itself done while announcing unperformed work, so 'done' means done.
Expected Behavior (from code): When a completion's tail announces future actions (first-person future + action verb) the loop injects one [harness] nudge per turn asking for the work or a plain finish; reporting language and 'I'll let you know' shapes do not match; both turn paths covered.

User Story: As an operator, I never want a veto-parrot cycle burning contexts, so a repeated completion is challenged instead of re-billed.
Expected Behavior (from code): A no-tool-call completion >=80 chars re-sent verbatim (whitespace-normalized) within one turn gets one escalating [harness] rail before any critic/quality spend; latches the struggle flag; both turn paths.

User Story: As a user, pasting docs that mention skills must not conscript the coverage backstop or plan seeder, so only real asks count.
Expected Behavior (from code): _skill_refs strips fenced blocks and quoted lines and only matches tokens prefixed by start/whitespace/comma/semicolon/bang; backticked/quoted/parenthesized/bracketed mentions are documentation.

User Story: As an operator on a small model, I want long skills turned into plan steps, so instructions get executed instead of recalled and dropped.
Expected Behavior (from code): use_skill bodies >=2000 chars return hint: FIRST decompose into update_plan steps folding in current context then execute in order (data decompose:true); short bodies keep the plain follow hint; tool description teaches the pattern once.

User Story: As an operator on a small model, I want a mutating apology spiral cut off like an exact loop, so a word swapped per line does not buy the model a screen of 'I will try to create the skill correctly'.
Expected Behavior (from code): repeated_tail convicts when >=8 of the last 15 lines are >=0.6 word-Jaccard to one line <=200 chars with >=3 distinct variants and fewer than half of the similar lines introducing a window-unique token (listings, code, checklists and identical-only windows under the exact bar are acquitted); same discard-retry-then-degenerated contract; the real 2026-08-26 wall convicts at the mid-stream probe.

User Story: As a user, I never want 'I have updated the file' accepted as done when no file changed, so a fabricated done gets challenged instead of completed.
Expected Behavior (from code): A completion whose tail reports a change (first-person past/perfect change verb tied to a file-ish object in the sentence) in a turn with zero executed non-READ_ONLY tool calls gets one [harness] nudge per turn and latches the struggle flag; a claim backed by a real write passes; the critic also runs on a quick_code turn whose completion claims a change; false-done regex now admits try to / attempt to / go ahead and / proceed to; the empty-completion nudge is a directive (one tool call, the answer, or one blocking sentence); both turn paths.

User Story: As an operator, I want a model that keeps answering nudges with words handed to the deep coder and told about, so the cheap model is not re-prompted forever in the dark.
Expected Behavior (from code): The second no-tool-call completion in a turn (necessarily after a nudge/veto) with no open plan latches the struggle flag (zakpick re-routes next iteration); a tool batch resets the count; streaming emits 'route: <category> -> <model>' on every route change and 'text-only completion #N (no tool calls)' status lines.

Feature: Skill intent via the classify side-call
User Story: As a user, I want 'finish forging this skill' held to the forging skill even though I never typed /forge-skill, so a request that names its skill in prose is not lost.
Expected Behavior (from code): DIFFICULTY_SCHEMA carries an optional skill (string|null); the side-call prompt lists the workspace catalog (name: description, capped) with a never-guess/null rule; parse_skill accepts only an exact catalog match; the loop's DifficultyVerdict feeds category to routing as before and, for a named skill, _adopt_implied_skill arms the coverage backstop and seeds the run /<skill> plan step (rebuilding the call so the step is visible immediately; streaming emits a status). Rides the existing side-call — no extra model call, no flag.

Feature: Typed /skill turns are not parsed as requests; blocker-without-evidence guard; anchored implied skills; route label names the model
User Story: As a user, I want /start sera to run the start skill — not seed 'run /stop' from its prose or load it twice — and a model that says 'I am blocked' to have actually tried something first.
Expected Behavior (from code): A user message beginning with the command-expansion frame is a composed skill turn: never seeded from, requested_skills empty (no second use_skill load). _execute_tool_call counts failed calls per turn; a first-person blocker claim in a completion's tail with zero failures gets one directive nudge (probe it or proceed) and latches the struggle flag. implied_skill_anchored requires a shared 4-char content stem between the request and the skill name/description or the classifier's skill is dropped. _provider_label unwraps .inner so status lines name the model.

User Story: As a user, I want a model that keeps re-running the same probe and seeing the same answer to be told so at the third time and lose the turn by the sixth — not spend 135 iterations and 103 minutes re-measuring.
Expected Behavior (from code): Fifth stuck signal repeated-outcome (stuck.py): (tool, file-edit epoch, normalized output with pids/times/hashes masked, >=24 chars) counted across the whole turn; the Nth identical observation lands on rung N of the existing ladder (3 nudge naming the count, 4 read-only, 5 step back, 6 stuck). The loop counts successful WORKSPACE_WRITE calls as the epoch, so edit->test->edit->test never reads as a repeat. No flag.

User Story: As a user, I never want the agent to delete or move .git, write into .git/, or permanently discard unreachable history, under any permission mode.
Expected Behavior (from code): DANGEROUS_PATTERNS gains: rm/rmdir/mv/shred/unlink/truncate of a .git path (relative or absolute; .gitignore/.github/.gitkeep exempt), shell redirects into .git/, git gc --prune=now, git prune (not prune-packed), git reflog expire --expire[-unreachable]=now. Rides the existing never-waivable blocklist (prompt in interactive modes, deny unattended).

User Story: As a user, I want a model that says a file could not be found to have actually searched for it by content first — grep, not me — before it asks for a path.
Expected Behavior (from code): A completion concluding could-not-find / not-found / does-not-exist with zero grep calls this turn gets one rail (_MISSING_NUDGE): grep by content and glob by path from the workspace root, then read what they find; never ask the user for a path not yet searched. Both loop paths; once per turn; a model that searched is never nudged.

User Story: As a user, when I say 'no way, go actually check', I want the previous figure re-measured with a tool call — not retracted with nine apologies that collapse into repetition.
Expected Behavior (from code): A user message disputing the previous answer (no way / are you sure / actually check / can't be right / prove it …) opens the turn with _CHALLENGE_RAIL: re-run the measurement, quote it, say whether the answer stands; 'go check the logs' is not a challenge; a first turn has nothing to contest. A no-tool-call completion carrying 3+ apology/retraction markers is discarded once (iteration refunded) behind _APOLOGY_NUDGE; a second rides the text-only stall.

Feature: Closest paths inside every not-found answer
User Story: As a user, I want 'File not found' to tell the model where that name DOES occur — by path and by content — so it reads the right file instead of giving up.
Expected Behavior (from code): read_file / list_dir / grep(path) errors and an empty glob append 'Closest paths by name:' and 'Files whose content mentions X:' from one ignore-aware, symlink-safe walk (40k entries / 2 s cap; data.suggestions carries both lists) plus a fix rail: read one of these, or grep+glob before concluding it is missing.

User Story: As a user, when I type /enocde-session I want /encode-session to run (and be told it was corrected), and a mistyped builtin to be suggested — never run.
Expected Behavior (from code): compose_skill_turn(fuzzy=True): a UNIQUE catalog neighbour at difflib ratio ≥ 0.8 runs, corrected_from rendered as '(you typed /enocde-session)'; ≥ 0.72 neighbours come back as suggestions when nothing ran. REPL order: exact skill → plugin command → fuzzy skill → 'unknown command /x — did you mean /y?' over builtins + skills. Builtins are never auto-corrected.

User Story: As a user, I do not want 'go actually try to fetch some of those' to seed a /research plan step because the word fetch appears in that skill's description.
Expected Behavior (from code): implied_skill_anchored: the skill NAME anchors on one shared 4-char stem; a DESCRIPTION anchors only on two distinct stems — one shared word with prose is a topic overlap, not a request to run the skill.

Feature: Evidence gates: identity claims and unsourced figures
User Story: As a user, when the model tells me what a path or skill IS, or how many of something there are, I want that backed by a tool call it made — not by memory of its own earlier writing.
Expected Behavior (from code): Identity gate: a no-tool-call completion asserting '<name-with-separator> is/was/is not (a|an) skill|script|file|module|directory|folder|package|executable' with no read_file/list_dir/glob/grep/use_skill this turn is asked once (_IDENTITY_NUDGE) to look. Figure gate: a comma-grouped or ≥4-digit number (years/dates/versions excluded) in a no-tool-call completion that appears in NO tool output and NO user message of the session is asked once to run the tool or state the provenance; assistant text is never a source. Both latch struggle, both loop paths.

User Story: As a user, when the model loads a skill I want it to see that a skill is a DIRECTORY — its path and the scripts beside SKILL.md — so it never tells me a skill 'is a python file'.
Expected Behavior (from code): use_skill appends '[skill directory] <workspace-relative dir>: <siblings>' (files and dir/, capped at 12, '(only SKILL.md)' when alone) to every loaded body; SkillLoad carries the SKILL.md path. The footer is the tool's own observation, outside the defanged body.

Feature: A Stop-hook veto opens a fresh skill turn
User Story: As a deployment running a perpetual loop (one /start, then Stop-hook vetoes without end), I want the re-entry the hook mandates to get the skill body it asks for, so a blocked turn-end can never become a dead loop.
Expected Behavior (from code): On a TURN_END veto the loop calls the Agent's per-turn skill reset (reload-dedup map cleared, invocation budget refilled) BEFORE the continuation prompt lands; the next use_skill of an already-loaded skill returns the body, never the '[already loaded]' pointer. Within an unvetoed turn the dedup still applies. Nothing is keyed on a skill name; a bare loop or sub-agent has nothing to reset.
Notes: ADR-0048. Measured 2026-08-26 (coach, zc-03, session 2fc9870): four vetoes each answered by the pointer, then the run ended and the agent stayed dark ~29h. Claude Code never dedups a Skill call; the Mind's own PreToolUse gate does and exempts aspirations|aspirations-*|worker-loop. Tests: test_a_stop_hook_veto_opens_a_fresh_skill_turn, test_no_veto_keeps_the_same_turn_dedup, test_turn_end_veto_calls_the_turn_reset, test_turn_end_allow_never_calls_the_turn_reset.

Feature: Self-restart into a newly installed build
User Story: As an operator, I want a running chat to pick up `zakcode update` by itself, so nobody has to remember to restart and no session keeps running stale code.
Expected Behavior (from code): build_info.install_identity() reads the install fresh (commit / checkout HEAD + the direct_url.json mtime marker); running_build() is that reading frozen at import; install_changed() compares markers only. The input mux polls the probe every 5s while idle (never mid-turn) and surfaces kind 'restart'; the REPL stamps Session.build with the new label, saves, and os.execv's python -m zakcode chat … --session <id> (chat named explicitly for the bare command); a failed exec is reported and the old process keeps serving; `zakcode update` announces the behavior instead of asking for a restart.

User Story: As a user, I want /resume to notice a transcript written by an older build or ended in a collapse, so the old failure does not replay into my new session.
